idea-plugin.name: KMP Dependency Hub
idea-plugin.description:
Every Kotlin Multiplatform dependency, one click away. Browse 4,800+ KMP, Compose Multiplatform and Android libraries inside Android Studio or IntelliJ IDEA, select several at once, and add them to the right place in your project.

Adding a library to a KMP project usually means: finding the latest version, putting the core artifact in commonMain, the right engine in androidMain and iosMain, adding Gradle plugins and KSP for every target, and hoping nothing Android-only ends up in commonMain. KMP Dependency Hub does all of that for you, and shows the diff before anything is written.

Features

  • Browse the top libraries from klibs.io, ranked by GitHub stars, in 22 categories (Networking, Database, DI, Navigation, Images, …). More load as you scroll.
  • Search klibs.io, Maven Central and Google Maven. New libraries appear as soon as they're published.
  • Recipes for popular libraries (Ktor, Koin, Room, SQLDelight, Coil, kotlinx, …) install everything they need: per-platform engines, BOMs, KSP processors for every target, Gradle plugins and config blocks.
  • Right source set, every time: commonMain, androidMain, iosMain, desktop and web, plus libs.versions.toml entries that reuse your existing aliases.
  • Platform-aware: libraries that don't publish for one of your targets are kept out of commonMain, before they break your iOS build.
  • Always current: the latest stable versions from Maven Central and Google Maven.
  • Review first: a diff of every change, applied as a single undoable action.
  • Doctor (Tools → KMP Hub: Run Doctor) flags incompatible commonMain dependencies, duplicates and available updates.

Getting started

  1. Open the KMP Hub tool window on the right.
  2. Browse a category or search, then tick the libraries you want.
  3. Pick the module (and, optionally, a source set), press Add, review the diff and apply.
  4. Sync Gradle.

Prefer the command line? The same engine ships as a Gradle plugin: kmpHubSearch, kmpHubAdd, kmpHubDoctor.
